Title
FY27 Nurse Educator Fellowship Program
Description
The purpose of the Nurse Educator Fellowship Program is to ensure the retention of well-qualified nursing faculty at institutions of higher learning that award degrees in nursing. Awards will be used to supplement the salaries of the nursing faculty selected for the Fellowship. Participation in this program is open to Illinois institutions of higher learning with a nursing program approved by the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation and accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) or the Association Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Nominations must be certified by the institution's Chief Nursing Administrator.

Other Submission Requirements
Each Fellow shall agree to: • Attend the recognition ceremony. • Collaborate with IBHE and Illinois Nursing Workforce Center in statewide nursing advocacy and attend fellowship meetings or associated conferences, as needed and with prior approval from their chief nursing administrator. • Provide a final abstract describing experiences and the use of funds. • Repay the fellowship if she/he terminates employment within six months after award notification. Each institution shall agree to: • Receive the award on behalf of the Fellow. • Use the funds solely to supplement the salary of the Fellow. First, all eligibility requirements of the institution and nominee must be met. Second, the following will be considered on a competitive basis: • Strength of the nomination by the chief nursing administrator. It is recommended to include the nominee’s major accomplishments, contributions, and involvement in programmatic and/or institutional efforts that contribute to the success of your nursing program. Note any doctoral degrees awarded. • Strength of the nominee’s personal statement regarding proposed use of funds, budget detail, and employment plans with the institution. In addition, consideration will be given to: • Statewide geographic distribution of fellowship recipients. • Equitable distribution of fellowship recipients among the nominations by degree levels and sectors of institutions. • Nominee’s tenure status (preference given to tenured/tenure-track faculty). • Proportion of the institution’s nursing students who are low-income, first-generation college, from rural communities, working adults, or students with disabilities and the institution’s success in reducing any equity gaps in nursing student enrollment and graduation. Student data previously submitted by the institution to IBHE will be used. • Pay the Fellow in accordance with institutional payroll policies and procedures. • Provide a financial report within 30 days after the Fellowship is paid to the Fellow. • Promptly refund any repayments made by the Fellow.

Question Submission Additional Information
As of October 2025, new Rules were approved by the Joint Committee on Administrative Rules (JCAR), and adopted by IBHE, implementing revisions to the Nurse Educator Fellowship award procedures, and meant to enhance the ability of eligible nursing faculty to benefit from the Fellowship program, including increased award amounts. 1. Under the new Rules, nursing faculty must now only wait 1 year before being able to reapply for a Fellowship award, instead of the previous 5-year wait provision. 2. Additionally, the new Rules now allow for a maximum award request of $25,000. Further guidelines for this provision are outlined under Attachment C criteria below. *Fellowship nominees may now request up to a maximum of $25,000 under the new Rules provisions. This is a competitive program. 3. Be employed in a nursing faculty position with a minimum of a .50 full-time equivalent at an eligible institution. Fellowship funds are salary supplements that, at the discretion of the Fellow, may be used for expenses related to professional development, conference expenses, continued education, professional dues, and travel to the recognition ceremony. Awards will be made to the nominating institution on behalf of the Fellow. The institution will pay the Fellow in accordance with the grant agreement and institutional payroll policies and procedures. Since the fellowship award is a taxable salary supplement the net payment after payroll deductions will likely be less than the requested amount. • The institution must pay the salary supplement to the Fellow upon notice of award and a signed Fellowship agreement with the IBHE. Please Note: The State Universities Retirement System (SURS) does not consider the fellowship award to be employee earnings that would impact retirement contributions for community colleges and state universities. SURS Legal Counsel found this payment as an award that is not associated with a particular time period and therefore not subject to SURS withholding. As such, this payment will not be included in the final rate of earnings and therefore, will not be included as earnings in the calculation of the 6% provision. (80 Ill. Adm. Code 1600.205(d)(3)(A)(ii))

Applicant Eligibility Information
Illinois resident with a minimum of a master's degree in nursing; employed in a full-time nursing faculty position at an eligible institution; employed by the nominating institution in a teaching position preparing registered nurses for a minimum of 12 months prior to nomination; made significant contributions to the nursing program; did not receive a fellowship within the past year (2026); nominated by the chief nursing administrator at an eligible institution.
Beneficiary Eligibility Information
N/A
Credentials Documentation Eligibility Information
N/A
Additional Eligibility Information
An eligible institution is an Illinois institution with a pre-licensure RN program approved by the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) and accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) or the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Fellowship nominations are limited to no more than three full-time nursing faculty members per eligible institution per year. An educator must meet the following qualifications before nomination by the chief nursing administrator: • Illinois resident with a minimum of a master’s degree in nursing. • Employed in a full-time nursing faculty position at an eligible institution. • Employed by the nominating institution in a teaching position preparing registered nurses for a minimum of 12 months prior to nomination. • Made significant contributions to the nursing program. • Did not receive a Nurse Educator Fellowship the previous year (2026). • Nominated by the chief nursing administrator at an eligible institution.

Other Information
Fellowship nominations are limited to a maximum of three nursing faculty members employed in a nursing faculty position with a minimum of a .50 full-time equivalent per eligible institution per fiscal year. A separate nomination with supporting documents is required for each nominee. 1. Chief Nursing Administrator makes the nomination to award an outstanding nursing faculty member. a. Write a letter as a nomination to recommend the nominee for the award. It is recommended to include the nominee’s major accomplishments, contributions, and involvement in programmatic and/or institutional efforts that contribute to the success of your nursing program. Note any doctoral degrees awarded 2. Nominee prepares supporting documents. a. Write a personal statement indicating intent to remain employed as a nursing faculty member. Please include a statement of your accomplishments, contributions, and involvement in programmatic and/or institutional efforts that contribute to the success of your nursing program. b. Prepare a budget of the anticipated use of funds to enhance teaching, learning, scholarship, student success, and/or professional practice. It is recommended that a budget includes a spreadsheet of proposed expenditures and an attached narrative of use of funds. c. Provide a resume or curriculum vitae. d. Give completed form and supporting materials to the Chief Nursing Administrator.

Criteria

Institutional Nomination

To what extent is the nomination supported by the institution’s chief nursing administrator (or dean/chair/supervisor when the nominee is the chief nursing administrator)?  (0-5 points)

 

To what degree does the nomination include the nominee's major accomplishments, contributions, and involvement in programmatic and/or institutional efforts related to nursing education? (0-10)

 

Tenure Status (maximum of 5 points)

Tenured/tenure-track = 5

No tenure system at the institution = 3 (New — previously these nominees scored 0).

Non-tenure-track at an institution that has a tenure system = 0



 

Nominee’s Personal Statement 

To what extent does the statement include the nominee’s major accomplishments and contributions in teaching/learning/scholarship/student success/professional practice? (0-15)

What indication is provided that the nominee intends to remain employed with the nominating institution if the fellowship is awarded?  (0-5)

   		 


 

Nominee’s Resume/Curriculum Vitae

What is the breadth and depth of the nominee’s major accomplishments and contributions to Nursing Education in areas such as teaching, scholarship, service, Program improvement, student recruitment and retention, and other special initiatives?  (0-20 points)

 

 

Proposed Use of Fellowship Award
   To what extent does the narrative and budget explain how
   the funds will be used to support the nominee’s
   professional development and growth? (Examples may  
   include: seminar and conference expenses, continued 
   education (e.g. degree/certification), professional dues,
   scholarship, travel to recognition ceremony). (0-10 points)

   How well does the proposed budget itemize and justify expenses in line with the requested award amount (e.g., registration/travel costs, titles and dates of each seminar/training/conference, tuition and instructional materials costs, degree-granting institution and program name)?  (0-10 points)

 

 


 


 

 

Review and Selection Process

First, all eligibility requirements of the institution and nominee must be met. 

 

Second, the following will be considered on a competitive basis:

  • Strength of the nomination by the chief nursing administrator. It is recommended to include the nominee’s major accomplishments, contributions to closing equity gaps, and involvement in programmatic and/or institutional efforts that contribute to the success of your nursing program. Note any doctoral degrees awarded.
  • Strength of the nominee’s personal statement regarding proposed use of funds, budget detail, and employment plans with the institution.

     

    In addition, consideration will be given to:

  • Statewide geographic distribution of fellowship recipients.
  • Equitable distribution of fellowship recipients among the nominations by degree levels and sectors of institutions.
  • Nominee’s tenure status (preference given to tenured/tenure-track faculty).
  • Proportion of the institution’s nursing students who are low-income, first-generation college, from rural communities, working adults, or students with disabilities and the institution’s success in reducing any equity gaps in nursing student enrollment and graduation. Student data previously submitted by the institution to IBHE will be used.
  • Pay the Fellow in accordance with institutional payroll policies and procedures.
  • Provide a financial report within 30 days after the Fellowship is paid to the Fellow.
  • Promptly refund any repayments made by the Fellow.           

Anticipated Announcement Dates

IBHE will score/review and select awardees as quickly as possible upon close of application deadline. Notifications will be provided to selected and non-selected applicants.
